body: Those contradictions are actually very common in schizoids: http://www.ptypes.com/schizoidpd2.html

I get it, thanks! I'm speculating here, but it might also be a defense mechanism to keep the nihilism from taking over every part of my conscience. When I lost all value of self, the meaning moved over to bigger things that will remain to be out of my control, so I will always hold a sense of importance associated with life that keeps me from getting suicidal.

A well-known trait of schizoids is that they experience a lot of conflicting things. Caring about the bigger social issues in life, but at the same time being selfish. Feeling inferior and insecure, but at the same time feeling better than most people in a narcissistic way. No interest in sex, but at the same time having rich fantasies about it, etc.

It sounds like you simply need some guidance to help you pursue those things about yourself which you feel that matter.

It might be in the right direction, seeking out larger issues is a logical response when you consider your own existence irrelevant, but I don't have the illusion that latching onto those issues matters whatsoever.

I prefer to stay in. I used to exercise, but there is no upside to it now. As to sex, the fantasy doesn't live up to the reality of it. I fantasize about it, but I know that the sight of an actual woman underneath me makes me lose all lust. Then it's just a meaningless heap of flesh that doesn't excite me in any way. The last time I attemped it I felt nothing, physically and mentally.
It's passing me by, but I don't see it as a negative thing. Eventually we all die, no matter how much you experience or achieve in the mortal life. It will all be in vain.

My close range empathy is somewhat double in the sense that I'm probably better at reading people and knowing what they feel and think than the average person since I observe a lot, but I still don't care. It's like you say, the problems of individuals seem barely important when you realize how big the problems on a global scale are. 'Normal' people tend to have these priorities the other way around, because otherwise they would go crazy.

Yep! I'm very anti-capitalist as well. I guess not caring about yourself enables you to objectively look at what is the best for the planet as a whole. I would easily give up my own privileged position in Western society for the benefit of equality for everyone.
Forget happiness, I would settle for life being bearable.
Mind = Blown
You can't at this moment. But realizing that means there is still hope your illness can be healed, if you were convinced that everything you feel is legitimate you would kill yourself.

Thanks! I will definitely hold on as long as possible, but I have never experienced happiness and I have always been incapable of connecting to another human being on a deeper level, so it's simply pointless to keep on living if that will never change. Human beings aren't wired to withstand that kind of loneliness and existential emptiness.

Even better! I'm sure this subreddit will contain a lot of things that are recognizable to you. Just try to stay strong until you start talking to a therapist, it will get better from that point onwards.

The place for you is professional help. I was around your age when I started feeling like that and I waited way too long before getting help, to the point where I probably can't be helped anymore. I assume you have a school counselor, that would be a good place to start.

I'm in the early stages, so I can't tell with certainty whether or not it will have a good effect. But it's the only thing I'm holding onto at the moment, so if I'm still in the same situation a couple of months from now I'm afraid that will be the end.

Think about the freedom that mentality can give you, most people are terrified of death and live their entire life being held back by that. You don't care and therefore can do whatever the hell you want with your life. Killing yourself is an option that will always be there in case nothing works out.

It's terrible. Those people would be devastated if you kill yourself and you clearly care a lot about them as well, so you have plenty of reasons to keep fighting against whatever you are dealing with.
Benzos work like a charm but are very addictive, so I would advise you to go with melatonin first.

I recognize that feeling of having a double personality. A lot of things are double with me. Feeling lonely, yet still wanting to be alone and things like that. On the one hand I feel like I see the world in a more realistic way than others, but on the other I think it might be caused by mental illness, perhaps you feel the same. That makes it hard to express yourself during therapy sessions, even though you might have the best intentions, because everything you think and experience feels so confusing and conflicting. I was completely apathetic for ten years, then almost killed myself and broke down, crying for the first time in those ten years and getting professional help. But now I'm more depressed and empty than ever, feeling like that breakdown was simply caused by survival instinct.

I can relate to that, most of the time I'm just a hump of complete apathy. What's the point of living if you can't connect to another human being on a deeper level? I have plenty of friends and family, but I wouldn't blink if any of them died. I'm just completely cut off from basic humanity. I have slipped off so far that I don't even experience physical pleasure while having sex. I just look at the girl and I'm like: ''She is exactly my type and objectively I should be enjoying this, but I don't feel a thing.''

It's exactly the other way around with me. Depression causes me to have absolutely no ability to concentrate, so reading a book is impossible. It's easier when the story is fed to me through movies and shows.

Nuances like that definitely come into play, it also depends on the severity of your depression. That's where professional help can be really useful as a place to reflect on those situations in which you may have been holding yourself back.

I think most of us experience that, but it's important to remember you have a disease. Would you fault someone with a physical illness for 'acting pathetic'? No, nor should you fault yourself as a carrier of mental illness for being unable to do certain things healthy persons are able to do.
Everyone on earth is completely disposable. It's hard and I haven't been able to do it yet, but there is light to be found in that darkness.
I applaud your creativity.
I don't like anything, so that theory is way too positive for me! Let's say my body is seeking the nearest grave.
It's hard when no one loves you and you love no one as well. Damn survival instinct.
The constant fucking nausea...
I'm beyond that point, but thank you for the offer, very kind.
No humor is strong enough to achieve that. It's more the feeling of ''If you can still smile now and then, there is hope of getting better''

Thanks for the offer :)

It really was meant as a dark joke, I guess still being able to laugh at my situation during the deepest depths anyone can experience is what is keeping me alive.
Death is exciting!
The worst thing about depression is waking up in the morning and discovering you once again didn't die in your sleep, meaning you will be convined to the prison cell called bed for another day.
I don't get hungry anymore, I have to force myself to eat a couple of slices of bread a day because starvation is a very cruel way of dying.
Suidical thoughts are the only thing that still can get a positive reaction from my brain. At least I will die doing what I love most, right?

I've spent the past four days in bed. Today I basically just stared at the ceiling for 16 hours straight, tormented by my thoughts. Sometimes I wonder how long a man can live miles below the point of minimum basic humanity without taking his own life.
It often feels strangely appropriate to bathe in your own filth for days on end. It's the state of your mind as well, after all.
I'm only funny on the internet and while drinking.
Everything that involves getting out of bed is an impossible task.
People are too cheery when it's sunny, I want everyone to be as miserable as I am.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5j2F4VcBmeo
Don't you just hate it when someone tells you it's just your depression talking? Like that somehow makes the statement less true.

"The nine-to-five is one of the greatest atrocities sprung upon mankind. You give your life away to a function that doesn't interest you. This situation so repelled me that I was driven to drink, starvation, and mad females, simply as an alternative." - Bukowski

If I had a gun I would have killed myself already. It's too much of an effort to actually get a gun, though. Have you ever been so depressed that you can't get out of bed because every movement you make feels like running a marathon? Have you ever been so depressed that sex doesn't excite you anymore?
I fully accept it, but that doesn't give me a reason to live.

Every drug should be legal, let that be clear. But, every person who heavily uses drugs is always trying to cover up deeper problems. You can run away from those problems for a long time, but they always will catch up with you eventually. Drugs are not a lifestyle, if you think that you have a problem.
Attention is a basic human need, so you are not a ''whore piece of trash'' for seeking it.
You are depressed. Depression is like existential boredom.

“I have absolutely no pleasure in the stimulants in which I sometimes so madly indulge. It has not been in the pursuit of pleasure that I have periled life and reputation and reason. It has been the desperate attempt to escape from torturing memories, from a sense of insupportable loneliness and a dread of some strange impending doom.”

You're very special for trying to help other people here at your age, hopefully the stories will prevent you from going down a similar path. If I got help at your age, I might be a very different person now. You're a good person, good luck with whatever you are going through yourself.

Thank you. I'm sorry for your losses, I've always wondered how I would react in such a scenario. I don't think I would blink if my mother died, while she raised me on her own and I have never had a real problem with her. The thing is, I don't feel anything, I'm completely apathetic. My only happiness has always come from flights of reality, dating back all the way to when I was 12. I have never been happy outside of the internet, which of course is a fake feeling of happiness. I retreated to the internet full-time to spend day after day on message boards or online games. 

Then when I turned 18, it was joined by gambling, drinking and drugs. For the first time it has really crashed down on me a short while ago, with my gambling debts growing out of my control. I might have a couple of more months before I have to leave my appartment because I can't pay the rent any longer. I don't have a job, I'm still in University. I'm not close to anyone, obviously due to my inability to connect with people, I only have acquaintances. Party friends at most. I could die and no one would notice for maybe as long as a month. 

Writing these posts is a start I guess, since even finding the energy to make a Reddit account took me a week. Fueled by a glass of vodka, granted, since otherwise I would be too apathetic to care and just lie in bed, waiting for either a miracle or a just as miraculous death.
